title: How to Attest Documents for Bangladesh: Embassy, MOFA and Notary Guide for Expats
metaTitle: Document Attestation for Bangladesh: Embassy, MOFA and Notary Guide
metaDescription: Step-by-step guide to attesting documents for use in Bangladesh and abroad: notary, foreign ministry legalisation, Bangladesh Embassy attestation and MOFA in Dhaka.
heroIntro: Whether you are sending a Power of Attorney from London, using a Bangladeshi degree in Dubai or submitting a marriage certificate in Toronto, the document has to be attested so that the receiving authority trusts it. A missing stamp can delay a property deal, visa or court case by months. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help you can call the chamber on 01712655546 or WhatsApp the same number.

quickAnswer.heading: Attestation Basics
points: Attestation = a chain of official verifications confirming that the signature, seal or copy on a document is genuine.
For Bangladeshi documents used abroad: issuing authority, then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) in Dhaka, then often the destination country's embassy.
For foreign documents used in Bangladesh: local notary or authority, foreign ministry (if required) and then the Bangladesh Embassy/High Commission.
Certificates from education boards or universities usually need prior verification (e.g. Education Ministry or board) before MOFA.
Fees, forms and processing time vary: always check the current official guidelines.

toc: Attesting Bangladeshi Documents for Use Abroad
Attesting Foreign Documents for Use in Bangladesh

sections.content:
Attestation is the process of getting an official to certify that a signature, stamp or copy on a document is genuine. Each authority only certifies the one before it. This creates a chain that the final receiving authority can trust.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

• Notary public: verifies your identity and signature or certifies a true copy.
  • Apostille: a single certificate used between member countries of the Hague Apostille Convention. Check whether the specific country pair accepts it, because Bangladesh's position and the other country's rules affect the route.
  • Consular legalisation: where the foreign ministry and then the embassy of the destination country stamp the document in sequence.

Always ask the receiving authority which method it accepts before you spend money.

sections.h2: Attesting Bangladeshi Documents for Use Abroad
sections.content:
1. Get the original or a certified copy from the issuing authority (e.g. education board, university, Registrar, Union Parishad/City Corporation, court).
  2. For certificates: verify with the relevant authority. Education certificates normally need verification by the board/university and then the Ministry of Education.
  3. Submit to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) attestation section in Dhaka for the official attestation stamp.
  4. If the destination country requires it, take the document to that country's embassy in Dhaka for legalisation.
  5. Keep several certified copies for different uses.

Some documents (birth, marriage and death certificates) must also be in English or have a certified English translation.

sections.h2: Attesting Foreign Documents for Use in Bangladesh
sections.content:
1. Sign or obtain the document in front of a notary public, or get it issued by the competent authority.
  2. If required, have the foreign ministry (e.g. FCDO in the UK, the Secretary of State in the US, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in UAE) legalise the notary.
  3. Take it to the Bangladesh Embassy or High Commission for consular attestation.
  4. Courier to Bangladesh; your advocate presents it to the Sub-Registrar office, court, bank or ministry.

• Power of Attorney: see our PoA guide.
  • Marriage certificate: Bangladeshi Nikahnama usually needs Registrar attestation and then MOFA.
  • Birth certificate: use the English online birth registration certificate and have it attested.
  • Police clearance: the issuing police authority first, then MOFA/embassy as needed.
  • Court orders and judgments: certified copy from the court, then Law Ministry and MOFA before use abroad.

Documents not in English (or the language of the receiving country) must be translated by a certified or sworn translator. The translation is often attested together with the original. For use in Bangladesh, documents in English are generally accepted, but other languages require translation to Bangla or English.

• Skipping a level in the chain (for example, going straight to MOFA).
  • Using photocopies where originals are required.
  • Name mismatch between passport, NID and the certificate.
  • Expired or very old documents (clearances usually have a validity window).
  • Paying "agents" without checking the official fee and receipt.

• Ask your advocate for the exact attestation chain for your purpose before you start.
  • Scan every document and keep a digital copy.
  • Use trusted courier services with tracking.
  • Start at least 4-6 weeks before any deadline.
  • Keep contact details of the embassy consular section and book appointments online where available.

faqs.question: What is the difference between notarisation and attestation?
faqs.answer: Notarisation confirms identity and signature before a notary. Attestation is the wider chain of official verifications (notary, ministry, embassy) that makes the document acceptable abroad.

faqs.question: Where do I attest Bangladeshi documents in Dhaka?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) attestation section attests documents after the issuing authority or concerned ministry has verified them.

faqs.question: Does Bangladesh accept an apostille?
faqs.answer: This depends on the country pair and current rules. Ask the receiving authority and check with the Bangladesh Mission before relying on apostille.

faqs.question: How long does attestation take?
faqs.answer: It can take from a few days to several weeks depending on the country and the number of steps.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer for attestation?
faqs.answer: Not always, but a lawyer helps for legal documents like PoA, court papers and property documents to make sure the chain is correct.
